title: Oeufs sur le plat (Eggs on the Dish)

instructions.text: Heat butter in an egg dish until melted and covering the bottom.
Carefully break the eggs into the dish without bursting the yolks.
Baste the yolks with a little hot melted butter and salt slightly.
Push into a moderate oven until the whites are milky-white and set; serve immediately.
Melt half of the butter in the dish, break the eggs without bursting the yolks, and baste with remaining butter.
Cook until the whites are quite done and the yolks remain soft and glossy.
Garnish with a small grilled sausage between the yolks and surround with a thread of tomato sauce.

title: Oeufs au beurre noir (Eggs with Brown Butter)

instructions.text: Cook the eggs in a dish in the usual way until the whites are set.
Heat butter in an omelet-pan until browned and fragrant, and pour over the cooked eggs.
Rinse the pan with drops of vinegar and besprinkle over the eggs.
Garnish the bottom of a dish with spinach leaves stewed in butter.
Sprinkle thereon two pinches of grated cheese.
Break the eggs upon this garnish and cover them with Mornay sauce.
Glaze quickly in a fierce oven or under the salamander.
Fill a sauté-pan with salted and acidulated boiling water (one tablespoon of vinegar per quart).
Break the fresh eggs into the water one by one and keep at a gentle simmer for 3 minutes.
Lift the eggs with a skimmer and transfer to cold water to stop cooking.
Trim edges neatly and drain before dishing.
Plunge fresh eggs into boiling water and boil gently for 5 to 6 minutes according to size.
Immediately immerse in cold water to arrest cooking.
Shell the eggs carefully while submerged in cold water.
Plunge eggs into boiling water and keep boiling gently for 8 to 9 minutes.
Cool immediately in cold water to prevent yolks from discolouring.
Shell carefully and serve or prepare for garnishes.

title: Oeufs brouillés aux champignons (Scrambled Eggs with Mushrooms)

instructions.text: Mince fresh mushrooms and sauté in butter until tender.
Beat eggs with salt, melt butter in a thick-bottomed stewpan over gentle heat.
Cook eggs slowly while stirring continuously until creamy, finishing with cream and butter off the fire.
Fold in the cooked mushrooms and serve immediately in a warm timbale.

title: Oeufs brouillés au fromage (Scrambled Eggs with Cheese)

instructions.text: Beat eggs with seasoning and fold in freshly grated Gruyère and Parmesan cheese.
Cook in a thick saucepan with butter over very moderate heat, stirring constantly.
Finish with cream and fresh butter off the heat; dish immediately.

title: Oeufs brouillés aux truffes (Scrambled Eggs with Truffles)

ingredients.preparation_note: cut into dice and cooked in Madeira

instructions.text: Simmer diced truffles in Madeira until fragrant.
Scramble the seasoned eggs with butter over gentle heat, stirring constantly.
Fold in the diced truffles and finish with cream and butter.
Garnish with fine slices of truffle and serve in a warm timbale.
Warm the cooked chopped spinach with cream and butter; season to taste.
Beat eggs with salt, melt butter in the omelet pan until foaming.
Pour in eggs, stir and shake vigorously until soft and scrambled.
Spread creamed spinach in the centre, fold the omelet, and turn out onto a hot platter.
Finely chop parsley, chervil, chives, and tarragon leaves in equal proportions.
Add chopped herbs to the beaten eggs with salt.
Heat butter in the omelet pan, pour in mixture, shake and stir rapidly until cooked but soft.
Roll the omelet and transfer to an oval serving dish.
Cut leeks, carrot, onion, cabbage, parsley root, celery, and beetroot into julienne strips.
Stew the vegetables gently in butter without colouring.
Moisten with hot beef and duck consommé, bring to a gentle boil, and simmer for 40 minutes.
Skim carefully and serve hot with beetroot infusion.

ingredients.preparation_note: red part cut into small dice

instructions.text: Cut carrots, turnip, leeks, celery, and onion into small regular dice.
Stew gently in butter with a pinch of salt and sugar until tender.
Moisten with clear boiling consommé and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Skim off any fat and serve clear with chervil leaves.
Prepare vegetables cut in olive shapes or thick rounds and cook gently in consommé.
Braise cabbage separately in stock and drain well.
Dry bread crusts in the oven with a drop of broth until crisp.
Combine vegetables in boiling consommé and serve accompanied by toasted crusts.
Put beef, marrow bone, and chicken in an earthenware pot with cold water and salt.
Bring slowly to the boil, skim thoroughly, and add carrots, turnips, leeks, and celery.
Simmer very gently for three hours, skimming frequently.
Add separately parboiled cabbage during the last hour and serve directly from the pot.
Stew sliced carrots and chopped onion in butter with thyme for 20 minutes without colouring.
Add white consommé and rice, bring to a boil, and cook gently for 40 minutes.
Rub through a fine sieve or purée until completely smooth.
Reheat, whisk in remaining fresh butter off the heat, and serve with small croutons.

title: Potage Velours (Carrot Tapioca Soup)
source_recipe_title: PURÉE DE CAROTTES AU TAPIOCA, otherwise VELOURS

instructions.text: Prepare Crécy carrot purée and thin slightly with white consommé.
Sprinkle in tapioca and cook at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes while stirring.
Finish off the fire with fresh butter and cream, and serve warm.
Cook lentils with bacon, sliced carrot, onion, and broth until completely tender.
Rub the lentils through a sieve to produce a smooth purée.
Dilute to proper soup consistency with hot consommé.
Simmer for 10 minutes, finish with butter, and garnish with chervil.

title: Potage Saint-Germain (Green Pea Purée Soup)
source_recipe_title: PURÉE DE POIS FRAIS, otherwise SAINT-GERMAIN

instructions.text: Cook fresh peas quickly in salted boiling water and drain immediately.
Melt butter in a saucepan, sweat sliced white of leek, and combine with peas.
Pound in a mortar and rub through a fine sieve with white consommé.
Reheat without boiling, finish with fresh butter, and serve with chervil.

title: Potage Parmentier (Potato and Leek Soup)
source_recipe_title: PURÉE DE POMMES DE TERRE, otherwise PARMENTIER

instructions.text: Finely mince the white of leeks and fry gently in butter without colouring.
Add peeled quartered potatoes and white consommé; cook quickly until potatoes are soft.
Rub through a fine sieve, return to heat, and adjust consistency.
Finish with butter off the fire and sprinkle with chervil leaves.

title: Potage Waldèze (Tomato and Tapioca Soup)
source_recipe_title: PURÉE DE TOMATES AU TAPIOCA, otherwise WALDÈZE

instructions.text: Cook tomato purée with white consommé until well amalgamated.
Rain in the tapioca and cook at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Finish off the heat with pieces of fresh butter until smooth and glossy.
Prepare a fine Parmentier potato-leek soup base.
Cut carrots, turnips, and leeks into fine julienne strips and stew in butter until tender.
Combine the tender julienne vegetables into the hot Parmentier soup.
Simmer for 5 minutes and serve hot.
Brown diced bacon and onion in a saucepan, add diced carrots, celery, and cabbage.
Moisten with consommé and bring to a boil; add tomatoes and diced potatoes.
Add rice, peas, and cut french beans; simmer until rice and vegetables are cooked.
Serve accompanied by grated Parmesan cheese.

title: Sole Meunière Doria
source_recipe_title: SOLE MEUNIÈRE AUX CONCOMBRES, otherwise DORIA

ingredients.preparation_note: turned into olive shapes and stewed in butter

instructions.text: Shape cucumbers into olive forms and stew gently in butter until tender.
Dredge sole fillets in flour and fry in hot foaming butter until golden on both sides.
Dish fish, surround with stewed cucumbers, sprinkle with lemon juice and chopped parsley.
Pour hot brown butter over the fish and serve immediately.

title: Sole au Vin Blanc (Sole in White Wine)

instructions.text: Butter an oven dish, scatter with minced shallots, and arrange the sole fillets.
Moisten with white wine and fish stock, cover with buttered paper, and poach gently in oven for 10 minutes.
Drain poaching liquor into a saucepan and reduce by half.
Whisk in pieces of cold butter off the heat until creamy, coat fillets, and glaze lightly.
Place fresh cod in cold salted water and bring gently to a boil.
Simmer very gently for 10 to 12 minutes without boiling fiercely.
Drain carefully and transfer to a serving dish on a napkin.
Surround with freshly steamed potatoes and serve with melted butter and chopped parsley.
Season cod slices with salt and pepper, and brush generously with oil.
Cook on a moderate grill for 12 to 15 minutes, turning carefully once.
Dish on a warm platter, top with fresh butter, and garnish with lemon wedges.
Trim beef tournedos into round noisettes and season with salt and pepper.
Brush lightly with oil or melted butter.
Grill over a fierce, clear fire for 3 minutes on each side to keep interior juicy.
Transfer to a hot dish, top with fresh butter, and serve with watercress.
Sauté the tournedos in hot butter until browned on both sides and medium-rare.
Remove tournedos and keep warm; in same pan, fry minced shallots and sliced mushrooms.
Deglaze with white wine, reduce, and add demi-glace and tomato sauce.
Simmer for 3 minutes, coat tournedos with sauce, and serve immediately.
Fry round bread crusts in butter until golden and crisp.
Fry tournedos in butter quickly, keeping them medium-rare, and set on the croutons.
Briefly sear slices of foie gras in butter and place one atop each tournedos.
Crown with hot sliced truffles and coat with Madeira demi-glace reduction.

title: Sauté de Veau Chasseur (Veal Sauté Chasseur)

instructions.text: Cut veal into even pieces and brown briskly in butter in a sauté pan.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced shallots, cooking until golden.
Swill saucepan with white wine, reduce, then add tomato sauce and demi-glace.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until meat is tender; sprinkle with parsley.

title: Côtelettes à la Champvallon (Lamb Cutlets Champvallon)

instructions.text: Brown lamb cutlets quickly in butter on both sides without cooking through.
Stew sliced onions in butter until tender and transparent.
In a baking dish, arrange alternating layers of sliced potatoes, onions, and cutlets.
Moisten with boiling stock flavoured with garlic and thyme; bake for 1 hour until browned.
Sauté chicken pieces in equal parts butter and oil until golden on all sides.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced shallots; cook until softened.
Pour off excess fat, deglaze the pan with white wine, and reduce by half.
Add Chasseur sauce, simmer gently for 10 minutes until chicken is tender; finish with chopped herbs.
Season chicken suprêmes and arrange in buttered moulds or baking pan.
Surround with raw sliced mushrooms tossed lightly in butter.
Poach gently under buttered paper with chicken consommé and cream for 12 minutes.
Arrange on a platter, reduce cooking juices with cream, and coat the suprêmes.
Poach chicken suprêmes in a buttered pan with a tight lid until tender.
Dish suprêmes and lay fine slices of black truffle upon each.
Coat with Mornay sauce flavoured with chicken essence and glaze quickly.
Garnish with clusters of buttered green asparagus tips and serve.
